title: Zhuangzi Drums on a Pot After His Wife's Death
text:
When Zhuangzi's wife died, his friend Huizi came to offer condolences. He found Zhuangzi sitting with his legs sprawled out, drumming on an earthenware basin and singing.

Huizi was shocked. "You lived with her," he said. "She raised your children and grew old with you. It would be enough not to weep now that she is dead. But to beat on a pot and sing, isn't that going too far?"

Zhuangzi said it was not like that. When she first died, how could he not have grieved? But then he thought back to before her beginning. There was a time when she had no life, and before that no form, and before that not even breath. In the midst of the jumble of things, a change took place and there was breath; breath changed and there was form; form changed and there was life. Now there had been another change, and she was dead. It was like the turning of the four seasons, spring to summer, autumn to winter.

She was lying peacefully in the great room of the world. If he went on sobbing and wailing, he said, it would show that he did not understand anything about fate. So he stopped.
lesson: Grief is natural, but seeing a death as part of the larger pattern of life can loosen its grip over time. Mourning and acceptance can follow one another.
